trigger_ar: كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
before: ʿĀd are named among the destroyed peoples.
after: Their fate carries the explicit cause of rejecting the messengers.
reason: The Arabic كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ names the same people and says they denied the messengers. It makes the focus's historical example a warning about rejecting revelation, not only a visible ruin.

trigger_ar: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
before: Thamud are named beside ʿĀd.
after: The paired example includes Thamud's rejection of messengers as part of its history.
reason: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ directly names Thamud and their denial of the messengers. This supplies a specific history behind the focus's pair of peoples and their being diverted from the way.

trigger_ar: وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا فَٰرِهِينَ
before: Their dwellings are visible evidence.
after: The homes are understood as impressive dwellings hewn from mountains, whose builders' confidence did not preserve them.
reason: The address وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا identifies Thamud's homes as carved mountain houses. That concrete construction image gives مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ a rock-hewn form and sharpens the contrast between formidable homes and their later evidentiary remains.

trigger_ar: فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ
before: Thamud are one of the peoples whose dwellings remain evident.
after: Their visible aftermath belongs to a punishment that overtook them despite their built environment.
reason: فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ explicitly says punishment seized Thamud in the surrounding account. It moves the named people in the focus from surviving evidence back to the judgment that made their dwellings a warning.

trigger_ar: فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةًۢ بِمَا ظَلَمُوا۟
before: Their dwellings are clear to later observers.
after: The houses stand empty because of their wrongdoing, making the ruins a moral witness.
reason: فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةًۢ names their houses as vacant, and بِمَا ظَلَمُوا۟ ties that vacancy to wrongdoing. The Arabic makes the focus's visible dwellings a direct, empty-house testimony rather than a neutral landmark.

trigger_ar: سِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
before: The dwellings make the past evident to the audience.
after: The ruins can be approached as part of an instructed inspection of past offenders' fate.
reason: سِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ turns travel and looking into a way to learn how offenders ended. This is a broad inspection motif that supports the focus's witness role for the dwellings, though the verse does not name these two peoples or their homes.

trigger_ar: فَيَنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
before: Their dwellings preserve evidence of earlier peoples.
after: The remains join a wider lesson: peoples stronger and more industrious than the audience still met an end after messengers came with proofs.
reason: The call to فَيَنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ asks observers to inspect previous peoples' outcome. The same verse says they had greater strength, cultivated the land, and received clear proofs, so the focus's ruined dwellings testify that material achievement did not avert judgment.

trigger_ar: أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
before: The past is legible from the dwellings.
after: Inspection of earlier peoples' fate also points to the limit of their greater strength before God.
reason: أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ repeats the journey-and-observation route to past outcomes. Its added claim that those peoples were stronger gives a general warning alongside the focus, but it does not identify the particular dwellings as the object inspected.

trigger_ar: لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِم مُّصْبِحِينَ
before: The dwellings are evident to later viewers.
after: The warning can be encountered in passing, in the ordinary route through the places where a destroyed people lived.
reason: لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِم مُّصْبِحِينَ says the audience passes by them in the morning. That encounter-by-passing can activate the focus's visible-remains image, although this short verse does not itself name houses or say what is seen.

trigger_ar: وَءَاثَارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ
before: Their homes are surviving signs of earlier judgment.
after: The dwellings belong to a wider field of traces on earth left by stronger peoples seized for their sins.
reason: وَءَاثَارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ explicitly speaks of traces across the earth, while فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ gives the judgment behind them. The focus's مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ can be heard as one inspectable trace within that material record.

trigger_ar: وَءَاثَارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
before: Their deeds are the object Satan made attractive.
after: The works and traces of powerful former peoples fail to protect them from their end.
reason: This verse joins وَءَاثَارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ with فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ: visible traces remain, while what they earned brings no benefit. It adds a consequence to أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ, showing that accumulated works and worldly marks cannot save the people who made them.

trigger_ar: صَٰعِقَةًۭ مِّثْلَ صَٰعِقَةِ عَادٍۢ وَثَمُودَ
before: ʿĀd and Thamud are the paired historical example.
after: Their paired fate becomes a warning model for anyone who turns away.
reason: The phrase صَٰعِقَةًۭ مِّثْلَ صَٰعِقَةِ عَادٍۢ وَثَمُودَ names both focus peoples as the measure of a warned-against calamity. It turns their names from historical evidence into an explicit comparison for a future audience that may turn away.

trigger_ar: رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا فِىٓ أَيَّامٍۢ نَّحِسَاتٍۢ لِّنُذِيقَهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْخِزْىِ
before: ʿĀd are named as a destroyed people.
after: Their destruction is specified as a fierce wind and disgrace in worldly life, with an afterlife punishment also stated.
reason: The preceding naming of ʿĀd identifies the pronoun in 41:16, where رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا gives the concrete means of their destruction. The focus's bare name therefore carries a specific judgment history, including عَذَابَ ٱلْخِزْىِ rather than ruin alone.

trigger_ar: فَٱسْتَحَبُّوا۟ ٱلْعَمَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ
before: They had insight, yet were turned from the way.
after: The paradox is sharpened as a people who preferred blindness over guidance despite being shown guidance.
reason: فَٱسْتَحَبُّوا۟ ٱلْعَمَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ directly stages blindness chosen in place of guidance for Thamud. Beside مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ, the image makes perceptual capacity compatible with a willed failure to follow the way.

trigger_ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضًا مُّسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا عَارِضٌۭ مُّمْطِرُنَا
before: The dwellings make the outcome clear to observers.
after: ʿĀd misread a visible sign as welcome rain when it was the punishment they had demanded.
reason: The words فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ and قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا show ʿĀd seeing the cloud but identifying it wrongly. This supplies a perceptual counter-image to تَّبَيَّنَ: outward visibility alone did not ensure that they recognized what was coming.

trigger_ar: وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ سَمْعًا وَأَبْصَٰرًا وَأَفْـِٔدَةًۭ فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلَآ أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ
before: They are described as perceptive.
after: Hearing, sight, and hearts can be present without saving those who deny the signs.
reason: وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ سَمْعًا وَأَبْصَٰرًا وَأَفْـِٔدَةًۭ names the faculties, and فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُمْ says they did not avail the people of ʿĀd. This strongly activates مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ as a paradox of perceptive equipment that does not overcome denial.

trigger_ar: أَهْلَكْنَا مَا حَوْلَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ وَصَرَّفْنَا ٱلْءَايَٰتِ
before: The dwellings serve as nearby evidence.
after: They belong to a surrounding landscape of destroyed towns and repeated signs intended to bring people back.
reason: أَهْلَكْنَا مَا حَوْلَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ makes nearby destroyed towns part of the audience's warning horizon. It is a regional parallel to the focus's dwellings, though the verse does not identify those specific houses or peoples.

trigger_ar: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ دَمَّرَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ
before: Their homes make a former people's fate inspectable.
after: The inspection of previous peoples becomes a warning that God can destroy the deniers as well.
reason: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ calls for looking at earlier outcomes, and دَمَّرَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ states the fate plainly. This broadly reinforces the focus's evidentiary lesson but leaves the dwellings themselves unstated.

trigger_ar: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌۢ بِٱلْقَارِعَةِ
before: The focus couples ʿĀd with Thamud as visible historical examples.
after: The pair is also bound by their denial of the overwhelming event.
reason: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌۢ بِٱلْقَارِعَةِ places both names together and attributes denial to them. The next verse begins Thamud's destruction account, so this paired denial directly deepens the focus's shared warning frame.

trigger_ar: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِٱلطَّاغِيَةِ
before: Thamud are one of the named peoples whose dwellings are evident.
after: Their end is an overwhelming destruction, a specific fate behind the surviving evidence.
reason: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِٱلطَّاغِيَةِ names Thamud and says they were destroyed by the overwhelming calamity. It makes the focus's people-name carry a compact account of the judgment that left its mark.

trigger_ar: عَادٌۭ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِرِيحٍۢ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍۢ
before: ʿĀd are named among peoples whose ruins remain.
after: Their destruction is tied to a raging, intensely cold wind.
reason: عَادٌۭ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِرِيحٍۢ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍۢ explicitly binds the focus's ʿĀd to destruction by a violent wind. The detail makes the name itself summon the force behind the lost dwellings.

trigger_ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ
before: ʿĀd are named as a past people.
after: Their name invites the audience to consider what their Lord did to them.
reason: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ repeats the name ʿĀd and frames their fate as something to behold. This lightly echoes the focus's appeal to evident remains, although the verse does not specify what was done or mention the dwellings.

trigger_ar: وَثَمُودَ ٱلَّذِينَ جَابُوا۟ ٱلصَّخْرَ بِٱلْوَادِ
before: Their dwellings remain as testimony.
after: Thamud's history includes monumental work through the rock of the valley, sharpening the material setting of their homes.
reason: وَثَمُودَ ٱلَّذِينَ جَابُوا۟ ٱلصَّخْرَ بِٱلْوَادِ pairs Thamud with rock cut through in the valley. That stone-working image gives the focus's dwellings a geological dimension, even though this verse does not itself call the cut rock houses.

trigger_ar: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَىٰهَآ
before: Thamud are named as a destroyed people.
after: Their rejection is linked to rebellious transgression.
reason: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَىٰهَآ says Thamud denied because of their rebellion. It fills in the moral cause behind the people named in the focus and their diversion from the way.

trigger_ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُم بِذَنۢبِهِمْ فَسَوَّىٰهَا
before: Thamud's dwellings are the remaining sign of their fate.
after: The sequence links denial and the killing of the she-camel to a crushing judgment that leveled them.
reason: In the surrounding Thamud account, فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا leads to فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُم بِذَنۢبِهِمْ فَسَوَّىٰهَا. This gives the focus's named people a concrete chain from rejection to punishment and leveling.

trigger_ar: يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِىَ
before: What remains from the dwellings has become clear to the audience.
after: A weaker lexical echo places clarification in a request for a precise description.
reason: يُبَيِّن لَّنَا shares the clarity root family with تَّبَيَّنَ and concerns making something distinct. The cow-description exchange is unrelated to ruins or failed insight, so this is only a lexical reminder of clarification.

trigger_ar: وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ
before: Satan makes deeds attractive and turns the people away.
after: The focus's diversion is heard as following Satan's successive steps instead of entering peace fully.
reason: وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ directly names Satan and warns against following his steps. The image supplies a process for the focus's turning from the way: diversion proceeds through followed steps, rather than appearing as a single isolated act.

trigger_ar: مِّنْ ءَايَةٍۢ بَيِّنَةٍۢ وَمَن يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ
before: The dwellings have become a clear sign.
after: A clear sign can be followed by a changed response and severe consequence.
reason: The phrase ءَايَةٍۢ بَيِّنَةٍۢ and the warning شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ frame clarity followed by accountability. It is a broad parallel to the focus's visible proof and punished peoples, but this verse says nothing about Satan or path obstruction.

trigger_ar: زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا
before: Satan beautifies the people's deeds.
after: The beautification extends to worldly life itself for those who disbelieve.
reason: زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا uses the same beautification verb with this world as its object. It activates the focus's زَيَّنَ while widening the attractive surface from their deeds to the life surrounding them.

trigger_ar: قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىِّ
before: The dwellings have made the evidence clear.
after: Clarity is framed as a distinguishable split between right guidance and error.
reason: قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىِّ repeats the focus verb and names guidance as distinct from error. This makes the focus's visible clarity resonate with a moral distinction whose opposing side resembles the path from which its peoples were turned.

trigger_ar: ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ فَنَجْعَل لَّعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
before: The focus describes insight despite failure.
after: No additional sense is activated by this mutual imprecation passage.
reason: ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ فَنَجْعَل لَّعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ concerns a challenge between disputants. Its words do not connect to the focus's dwelling evidence, Satanic diversion, or the insight paradox.

trigger_ar: يَشْتَرُونَ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَن تَضِلُّوا۟ ٱلسَّبِيلَ
before: The people are barred from the recognized way.
after: Others can actively purchase error and want the audience to stray from that way.
reason: يَشْتَرُونَ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَن تَضِلُّوا۟ ٱلسَّبِيلَ turns deviation into an intentional project directed at other people. It activates ٱلسَّبِيلِ as the target of obstruction while adding human agents who want others to stray.

trigger_ar: فَمِنْهُم مَّنْ ءَامَنَ بِهِۦ وَمِنْهُم مَّن صَدَّ عَنْهُ
before: Satan turned the peoples away from the path.
after: The obstruction verb also describes a divided response, with some turning away from the messenger or message at issue.
reason: مَّن صَدَّ عَنْهُ uses the same root and away-from construction as فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ. The focus's obstruction thus resonates with a person's own turning away, although this verse does not name Satan as the agent.

trigger_ar: وَإِن يَدْعُونَ إِلَّا شَيْطَٰنًا مَّرِيدًا
before: Satan is the named beautifying agent.
after: The other passage describes Satan as a rebellious object of invocation, extending the focus's adversarial image.
reason: وَإِن يَدْعُونَ إِلَّا شَيْطَٰنًا مَّرِيدًا directly repeats the Satan figure and calls him rebellious. This is a real but limited activation: it does not describe beautification or specify a path from which people are turned.

trigger_ar: لَأَتَّخِذَنَّ مِنْ عِبَادِكَ نَصِيبًا مَّفْرُوضًا
before: Satan's work affects the named peoples.
after: His own declared aim is to claim a portion of God's servants.
reason: لَأَتَّخِذَنَّ مِنْ عِبَادِكَ نَصِيبًا مَّفْرُوضًا portrays Satan claiming a share among the servants. That supplies an adversarial aim behind the focus's Satanic action, though it does not state the particular method of beautifying or blocking.

trigger_ar: وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ
before: Satan beautifies deeds and obstructs the path.
after: Satan's own stated program includes leading people astray and filling them with hopes.
reason: وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ names Satan's intent to mislead, while وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ adds promises or wishful hopes as a means. The statement directly activates the focus's satanic diversion and gives an inner persuasive mechanism alongside beautified deeds.

trigger_ar: وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا
before: Satan's attractive framing leads the people away.
after: His promises are characterized as delusion, making apparent benefit itself unreliable.
reason: وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا calls Satan's promises delusion. It supports the focus's deceptive attractiveness, while stopping short of mentioning deeds or the path.

trigger_ar: لَا تَتَّخِذُوا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
before: The focus assigns Satan an adversarial role.
after: A separate warning concerns choosing protective allegiance on the wrong side.
reason: لَا تَتَّخِذُوا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ warns about misplaced allegiance. This only weakly touches the focus's adversarial-agent frame; it does not say that Satan beautifies deeds or diverts anyone from a path.

trigger_ar: أَخْذِهِمُ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ وَأَكْلِهِمْ أَمْوَٰلَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ
before: The focus concerns deeds made attractive and diversion from a way.
after: This passage names financial offenses and punishment without activating that image.
reason: أَخْذِهِمُ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ and أَكْلِهِمْ أَمْوَٰلَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ specify usury and wrongful consumption of wealth. The listed path-obstruction association is absent from these words, so the pairing is incidental.

trigger_ar: كَفَرُوا۟ وَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ قَدْ ضَلُّوا۟ ضَلَٰلًا بَعِيدًا
before: The path is what the people were turned away from.
after: Disbelief and blocking others from God's path end in far error.
reason: كَفَرُوا۟ وَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ repeats the path-obstruction pattern explicitly and follows it with far misguidance. It activates both ٱلسَّبِيلِ and فَصَدَّهُمْ in the focus, while naming a human group as agents of the same blocking.

trigger_ar: فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُۥ نَفْسُهُۥ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُۥ
before: The focus says Satan made the people's deeds attractive.
after: Here a person's own soul makes fratricide seem compliant or easy before he commits it.
reason: فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُۥ نَفْسُهُۥ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ depicts the self smoothing the way to a grave act. It is a strong rationalization image that can illuminate أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ under beautification, but its agent is the soul rather than Satan.

trigger_ar: وَأَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًا وَضَلُّوا۟ عَن سَوَآءِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
before: The focus says a people were turned from the path.
after: The other passage joins leading many astray with straying from the sound path themselves.
reason: وَأَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًا وَضَلُّوا۟ عَن سَوَآءِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ combines active misguidance of others and departure from a rightly balanced way. That closely activates the focus's path-diversion image, while extending it into a social chain.

trigger_ar: لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ
before: The focus attributes insight to people who nonetheless went astray.
after: The sight vocabulary raises a limit on what eyes can perceive.
reason: لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ repeats the eye and perception image beside مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ. The subject here is God's transcendence rather than human misjudgment, so the shared perceptual vocabulary is evocative but weakly connected.

trigger_ar: شَيَٰطِينَ ٱلْإِنسِ وَٱلْجِنِّ يُوحِى بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ زُخْرُفَ ٱلْقَوْلِ غُرُورًا
before: Satan makes deeds attractive and blocks the way.
after: Devils exchange ornamented speech as deception, another crafted surface that can entice people away.
reason: شَيَٰطِينَ ٱلْإِنسِ وَٱلْجِنِّ are agents of زُخْرُفَ ٱلْقَوْلِ غُرُورًا, ornamented speech used deceptively. This strongly activates وَزَيَّنَ through the shared image of beautification, while shifting its object from deeds to persuasive words.

trigger_ar: وَلِتَصْغَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَفْـِٔدَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا۟
before: The focus links beautified deeds with diversion.
after: Hearts incline to an enticing object, accept it, and proceed to commit acts.
reason: وَلِتَصْغَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَفْـِٔدَةُ and وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَ لِيَقْتَرِفُوا۟ trace inclination into acceptance and action. With the ornamented speech of 6:112 as the antecedent, this shows how seduction can issue in deeds, though the quoted ayah does not itself name beautification.

trigger_ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآئِهِمْ لِيُجَٰدِلُوكُمْ
before: Satan is the source of the focus's diversion.
after: The plural devils inspire their allies to argue, giving another form of adversarial influence.
reason: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآئِهِمْ attributes inspiration to devils and directs it toward argument. This activates the focus's Satanic-agent sense, but does not reproduce its beautification or path image.

trigger_ar: لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ
before: The focus says Satan turned the peoples from the way.
after: Satan describes himself as taking a position against them on the straight path.
reason: لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ places Satan directly on the route of the straight path in order to waylay people. It turns the focus's abstract diversion from ٱلسَّبِيلِ into an image of adversarial interception.

trigger_ar: وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا
before: The focus names ʿĀd among the peoples with evident dwellings.
after: Their prophetic history includes Hud's call to worship God and be mindful.
reason: وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا identifies Hud's address to ʿĀd, and ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ states its demand. This gives context for the focus's named people, but the cited words do not record their rejection or destruction.

trigger_ar: جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ
before: The focus recalls a people who had insight yet failed.
after: The associated address reminds a later generation of its succession, strength, and divine favors.
reason: جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ and زَادَكُمْ فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ بَصْطَةًۭ situate the addressed people in a powerful succession, followed by a call to remember God's favors. This gives the named Aad narrative a warning context, but the cited ayah has not yet stated their response to the reminder.

trigger_ar: فَأَتْبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْغَاوِينَ
before: The focus says its peoples were perceptive but were diverted.
after: A recipient of signs sheds them, is pursued by Satan, and becomes one of the strayers.
reason: فَأَتْبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْغَاوِينَ links Satan to a fall into error after the person has been given signs. It supplies a close parallel to insight or evidence coexisting with Satanic diversion, without equating the two people's stories.

trigger_ar: وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ نَزْغٌۭ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ
before: Satan beautifies deeds and turns people away.
after: His assault is also described as a prompting or incitement that calls for refuge in God.
reason: يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ نَزْغٌۭ names an incitement from Satan, giving the focus's agent a more immediate mode of influence. The verse does not connect that prompting to beautified deeds or a blocked path, so the activation remains partial.

trigger_ar: وَإِخْوَٰنُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِى ٱلْغَىِّ ثُمَّ لَا يُقْصِرُونَ
before: The people are turned away from the path.
after: Their companions keep extending them in error without stopping.
reason: يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِى ٱلْغَىِّ describes associates actively carrying others further into error, and ثُمَّ لَا يُقْصِرُونَ says they persist. It gives the focus's obstruction a continuing social mechanism, even though the agents here are companions rather than Satan himself.

trigger_ar: كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ
before: The focus names particular peoples as historical evidence.
after: A broader precedent joins rejection of signs to being seized for sins.
reason: كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ followed by فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ supplies a general pattern of denial and judgment. It echoes the focus's warning function, but this verse does not identify ʿĀd or Thamud or their dwellings.

trigger_ar: بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا مُّجْرِمِينَ
before: The focus's people had perceptual capacity but went astray.
after: A different audience receives signs and responds with arrogance and criminal conduct.
reason: بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ gives a pattern of signs followed by pride, which can accompany the focus's contrast between evidence and failed response. The verse is about Pharaoh's circle and does not name the focus peoples, so its contribution is a broad parallel only.

trigger_ar: أَن يُصِيبَكُم مِّثْلُ مَآ أَصَابَ قَوْمَ نُوحٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ هُودٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ صَٰلِحٍ
before: The focus names ʿĀd and Thamud as ruined precedents.
after: The warning identifies the peoples of Hud and Salih as possible fates for those who oppose their messenger.
reason: قَوْمَ هُودٍ and قَوْمَ صَٰلِحٍ evoke the communities associated with ʿĀd and Thamud, while أَن يُصِيبَكُم مِّثْلُ مَآ أَصَابَ frames their fate as a warning. This joins the two named focus peoples through their prophets and supplies a direct consequence for rejecting a messenger.

trigger_ar: وَأُتْبِعُوا۟ فِى هَٰذِهِۦ لَعْنَةًۭ وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
before: The focus says a people were diverted from the way.
after: The prior narrative's followers are pursued by a curse in this life and the Day of Resurrection.
reason: وَأُتْبِعُوا۟ فِى هَٰذِهِۦ لَعْنَةًۭ depicts an enduring consequence following a people, extended to the Day of Resurrection. It can accompany the focus's account of destructive following, but the cited line itself does not state the diversion or name ʿĀd and Thamud.

trigger_ar: سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا
before: Satan made the people's deeds appear attractive.
after: A self can also make a wrongful matter seem acceptable, exposing an inward form of rationalization.
reason: سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا attributes a made-acceptable story to the brothers' own selves. This is a strong Quranic usage parallel to وَزَيَّنَ, while moving the focus's beautification from an external Satanic agent to internal self-persuasion.

trigger_ar: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
before: The dwellings let later audiences see a prior fate.
after: Travel and looking at earlier peoples' outcomes is presented as a route to recognize the lesson and consider the next life.
reason: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ asks for the same general inspection of earlier outcomes implied by the focus's evident dwellings. Its reference to the better final abode adds an afterlife frame, but the specific ruins are not named.

trigger_ar: لِّيُضِلُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ
before: Satan turned the peoples away from the way.
after: People who set up rivals for God may themselves act to mislead others from His path.
reason: لِّيُضِلُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ explicitly names the purpose of leading others from God's path. This activates ٱلسَّبِيلِ and the focus's diversion pattern, while shifting agency from Satan's beautification to idolaters' intentional misleading.

trigger_ar: ٱتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا
before: The ruined dwellings remain as evidence of a people's fate.
after: The surah's later spider-house parable makes dwelling a possible image of failed shelter: a house can look like refuge yet be weak.
reason: مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ in the focus and بَيْتًا / أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ in 29:41 share the explicit habitation image. Read together, the visible homes of the destroyed peoples can recall the later parable's fragile shelter and the false security of protection taken apart from God.
